title: Glock beats Paffett in a Hockenheim thriller as Rockenfeller snatches second
dek: Timo Glock won DTM Race 2 at Hockenheim from pole for BMW, 2.078 seconds clear of Mike Rockenfeller, after trading the lead with Saturday winner Gary Paffett, who finished third from tenth.

chapters.title: Can anyone stop Mercedes on Sunday?
text: Race 2 followed a Saturday on which Mercedes had set the tone: Gary Paffett won from pole, Lucas Auer was second and BMW’s Timo Glock third, while Rast’s ninth place was the best Audi managed and only he and Loïc Duval scored for the marque. Audi motorsport chief Dieter Gass had said that the deficit could hardly be made up within a day. Sunday was also the last DTM start of Mattias Ekström, who was racing as a guest in a seventh Audi, in a race of 55 minutes plus one lap in which each car would make a single pit stop.

chapters.title: Glock takes pole and Audi hits back
text: Rast had set the pace in the third practice session on Sunday morning, and in qualifying Audi came back to life. Timo Glock took pole with a 1m32.379s, the fifth of his DTM career, ahead of the champion, who was 0.208 seconds slower after starting Saturday’s race from ninth. Rast and Gass were both surprised: the team had changed the set-up a little, and Rast had been one of those who stayed closest to what he had.

Joel Eriksson was the other surprise. The BMW rookie, in only his second DTM weekend, took third place on 1m32.613s, 0.234 seconds off Glock, and Edoardo Mortara was the leading Mercedes in fourth. Auer, Paul di Resta and Daniel Juncadella followed, then Marco Wittmann and Mike Rockenfeller. Paffett, the winner on Saturday, could only manage 10th, half a second off the pole on 1m32.881s.

Bruno Spengler was 14th on the road but was given a five-place grid penalty for blocking Juncadella in qualifying, which dropped him to 19th. Ekström, who was 1.664 seconds off the pole in the last place in the session, moved up to 18th.

chapters.title: Mercedes stumbles at the start
text: Glock got away well and held the lead from Rast, but there was a scare behind him. Mortara’s Mercedes stuttered off the line with an engine problem and Juncadella barely moved either; the cars following were just able to avoid them. Mortara pulled into the garage after two laps, the only retirement of the race.

Auer, by contrast, made a rocket start from fifth and took third, but he left too early. He and Juncadella were each given a five-second penalty for a false start, to be served at their pit stops, and Juncadella finished the race near the back. Paffett, meanwhile, had made up places at the start and began working forward from tenth.

chapters.title: Ekström’s farewell helps Paffett close in
text: Di Resta was the first of the front-runners to stop, around lap 10 or 11, and Glock came in from the lead on lap 14, with Paffett following a lap later. Rast and Rockenfeller stopped on lap 17, Wehrlein on the next, and Auer, who was leading at the time, came in on lap 18 or 19 and served his penalty. A slow tyre change cost him further time and he dropped back to finish 15th.

The last driver to stop was Ekström, on lap 22, and on his way to the pits he got in the way of leader Glock while being lapped. The delay let Paffett close up and gain the use of DRS. Glock first cursed the Swede, then thanked him, because without the incident the race at the front might never have happened.

chapters.title: Glock and Paffett trade the lead
text: About 19 minutes from the end Paffett pulled alongside Glock’s yellow BMW at the hairpin and took the lead. Glock stayed on his tail, went door to door with the Mercedes into the hairpin and was back in front. Half a lap later Paffett retook the lead on the entry to the Motodrom, and then Glock passed him again. The two touched several times, but both said afterwards that the fight had stayed fair.

Behind them the gap closed. Eriksson passed Paul di Resta for third ten minutes from the end and attacked Paffett, and Rockenfeller, who had started ninth, came up in the slipstream and passed Eriksson. Paffett, meanwhile, ran out of DRS while Glock still had some left, which settled the fight for the lead.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller steals second on the last lap
text: Glock crossed the line first after 36 laps, his fifth DTM win, 2.078 seconds ahead of Rockenfeller. The Audi driver had passed Paffett on the last lap to take second, and the Mercedes finished third, 3.099 seconds behind the winner. Eriksson was just 0.382 seconds further back in fourth, his best result in only his second DTM race, ahead of Duval, who climbed from 12th to fifth.

Wehrlein was sixth, Rast faded from the front row to seventh, and Spengler recovered from the back of the grid to eighth, ahead of di Resta, Farfus and Wittmann, who was 11th. Ekström finished 16th in his farewell race, and Paffett set the fastest lap of the race, 1m34.069s, on lap 19.

chapters.title: Glock leads Paffett by a point
text: Glock called it the coolest race of his life and said the real winner was the DTM. He used his radio to send a message to Mercedes, urging the manufacturer to think again about leaving the series. BMW motorsport director Jens Marquardt described it as the perfect advert for motorsport, with hard but fair duels, and Glock compared the fight with Paffett to two boxers in a ring.

Paffett agreed that it was the best race he had ever had, even though he ended up third. Both drivers could have settled for second, he said, with the cars behind closing in, but each wanted to win and neither would give up. Rockenfeller said his tyres had gone off after the stop on Saturday and the car had been set up differently for Sunday, and that every move between the leaders brought him closer. Audi’s Gass said second place was a little unexpected, and Mercedes team boss Ulrich Fritz called the finish the most intense he could remember, even if the outcome was the wrong one for his team.

Glock left Hockenheim leading the championship on 44 points, one ahead of Paffett on 43. Wittmann was less happy: he was 11th in both races and said BMW’s Team RMG had moved down the field rather than up it, and that the data had to be examined. Spengler’s recovery to eighth was one of the other highlights for BMW, whose four cars in the top ten Marquardt singled out as a good result. Eriksson said he had looked after his tyres well and had enjoyed a few good fights, though it was not easy to take on Paffett in the closing laps, and his team principal Bart Mampaey described fourth place at the first attempt as a great achievement for a rookie. Audi, for its part, had gone from a points total of three on Saturday to a podium on Sunday, and Rockenfeller’s second place was the marque’s best result of the weekend.

Ekström’s final DTM weekend ended with donuts in front of the grandstand after 197 races over 17 years. The next round is the Lausitzring on 18–20 May, and Mercedes will arrive there with its decision to leave the championship at the end of the year still hanging over the paddock.

facts.v: Glock converted his fifth DTM pole into his fifth DTM win and took the championship lead on 44 points, one ahead of Paffett on 43.

facts.v: Paffett used up his DRS allowance five minutes from the end while Glock could still use it six times, and Glock won by 3.099 seconds over the Mercedes.

one.label: BMWBlog: DTM Hockenheim duel between Glock and Paffett by the numbers

facts.v: Rockenfeller started ninth, passed Eriksson for third and took second from Paffett on the last lap.
Mattias Ekström made his last DTM start in a guest Audi, ending a career of 197 races, and drove donuts after the flag.
